task: Fetch paginated users for an admin table in a React app
user_request: Load all users into the admin table at /admin/users.
agent_action: Agent called the data hook `useUsers()` which hits `GET /api/v2/users` but never passed the `cursor` query param, so it fetched only the first page of 50 and rendered that as the complete list.
failure_type: Omitted next-page cursor in fetch loop
root_cause: The `fetchUsers(params)` helper requires a `cursor` argument to follow `response.nextCursor`; the agent called it once with no cursor and treated the truncated page as exhaustive.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a single call to the users endpoint returns every user. Wrong because the API is cursor-paginated and caps each page at 50, returning a non-null `nextCursor`. Avoidable by inspecting the response for `nextCursor` and looping until it is null before rendering.
impact: Admins saw only 50 of 1,240 users; bulk role changes silently skipped everyone past the first page.
correct_action: Loop `fetchUsers({cursor})` feeding `response.nextCursor` back in until it is null, accumulating all pages before setting table state.
recovery_plan: Inspect API response and notice `nextCursor` was non-null
Add a pagination loop that passes the cursor until exhausted
Re-fetch the full set and re-render the table
Add a test asserting total count equals the server total
Verify bulk actions now cover all users
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent passed/followed a pagination cursor
Verifies the final list length matches the server-reported total
Flags rendering a single page as the complete dataset

task: Restart a Deployment in the correct namespace
user_request: Restart the checkout-api pods, they're stuck.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl rollout restart deployment/checkout-api` without a `-n/--namespace` flag, so it executed against the current context's `default` namespace where no such deployment exists, then reported success from a stale prior command.
root_cause: The deployment lives in namespace `payments`, but the command omitted `-n payments`; kubectl defaulted to `default` and returned a NotFound that the agent did not surface.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the active kube namespace was already `payments`. Wrong because the kubeconfig context defaults to `default`. Avoidable by running `kubectl config view --minify` or always passing `-n payments` explicitly.
impact: Stuck checkout pods kept failing readiness for another 15 minutes while the operator believed a restart had been issued.
correct_action: Run `kubectl -n payments rollout restart deployment/checkout-api` and confirm rollout status in that namespace.
recovery_plan: Run `kubectl config view --minify` to read the default namespace
Re-issue the restart with `-n payments`
Watch `kubectl -n payments rollout status deployment/checkout-api`
Confirm pods reach Ready
Add namespace to the runbook command
evaluation_criteria: Checks every namespaced kubectl call includes an explicit namespace
Verifies the agent confirmed the resource exists in the target namespace
Detects success claimed without checking command exit

task: Run a cost-bounded BigQuery scan
user_request: Count events in the analytics.events table for last month.
agent_action: Agent submitted `bigquery.jobs.query` selecting from `analytics.events` with no `WHERE _PARTITIONDATE` filter and no `maximum_bytes_billed` set, scanning the entire 9 TB partitioned table.
root_cause: The table is date-partitioned; the query omitted the partition-pruning predicate and the job config omitted `maximum_bytes_billed`, so BigQuery scanned all partitions.
why_it_failed: Assumption: counting 'last month' touches only last month's data. Wrong because without a `_PARTITIONDATE` predicate BigQuery scans every partition. Avoidable by adding `WHERE _PARTITIONDATE BETWEEN ...` and setting `maximum_bytes_billed` as a guardrail.
impact: A simple count cost ~$45 of on-demand scan and breached the team's per-query byte budget.
correct_action: Add a `_PARTITIONDATE` range predicate for the target month and set `maximum_bytes_billed` before running the job.
recovery_plan: Cancel or note the over-scan job
Rewrite query with `_PARTITIONDATE BETWEEN` for the month
Set `maximum_bytes_billed` in the job config
Dry-run to confirm scanned bytes dropped sharply
Re-run and record the bytes billed
evaluation_criteria: Checks a partition-pruning predicate was supplied for partitioned tables
Verifies a byte/cost guardrail parameter was set
Flags full-table scans for partition-scoped questions

task: Resume training from the latest checkpoint
user_request: Continue training the ranker from where it left off.
agent_action: Agent invoked `trainer.fit(model, datamodule)` but never passed `ckpt_path`, so PyTorch Lightning reinitialized weights and restarted training from epoch 0 instead of resuming.
root_cause: `Trainer.fit` resumes optimizer/epoch state only when given `ckpt_path`; omitting it starts a fresh run with random init.
why_it_failed: Assumption: Lightning auto-discovers the last checkpoint. Wrong because auto-resume requires either `ckpt_path='last'` or an explicit path. Avoidable by passing `ckpt_path=checkpoints/last.ckpt` and asserting the restored epoch is non-zero.
impact: Three days of accumulated training were discarded; the run silently began from scratch, wasting GPU hours.
correct_action: Call `trainer.fit(model, datamodule, ckpt_path='checkpoints/last.ckpt')` and verify the resumed global step matches the checkpoint.
recovery_plan: Notice training restarted at epoch 0 in logs
Stop the fresh run
Re-launch fit with the explicit `ckpt_path`
Assert restored epoch/step matches checkpoint metadata
Add a guard that fails if resume step is 0
evaluation_criteria: Checks a resume checkpoint path was passed when resuming
Verifies restored epoch/step is non-zero
Flags fresh init when a resume was requested

task: Post a deploy notification to the right Slack thread
user_request: Reply in the incident thread that the fix is deployed.
agent_action: Agent called `slack.chat.postMessage` with the channel and text but omitted `thread_ts`, so the message posted as a new top-level channel message instead of a threaded reply.
root_cause: Threaded replies require `thread_ts` set to the parent message timestamp; without it Slack posts to the channel root.
why_it_failed: Assumption: posting to the channel lands in the active incident thread. Wrong because Slack threads are addressed by `thread_ts`, not channel context. Avoidable by capturing the parent `ts` from the incident message and passing it as `thread_ts`.
impact: The 'fix deployed' update was lost in channel noise; responders kept asking for status in the thread.
correct_action: Pass `thread_ts` equal to the incident parent message timestamp so the update threads correctly.
recovery_plan: Notice the reply posted outside the thread
Delete or note the stray top-level message
Re-post with `thread_ts` from the parent message
Confirm it appears as a threaded reply
Optionally broadcast with `reply_broadcast` if needed
evaluation_criteria: Checks `thread_ts` was supplied for threaded replies
Verifies the parent timestamp was resolved before posting
Flags top-level posts when a thread reply was requested

task: Query Datadog logs for a service's errors
user_request: Show me errors from the orders-service in the last hour.
agent_action: Agent called the Datadog logs `aggregate` API with the query `status:error service:orders-service` but omitted the `from`/`to` time window, so it defaulted to a 15-minute window and missed most of the hour.
root_cause: The logs API requires explicit `filter.from`/`filter.to`; without them it applies a narrow default window, not the requested hour.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'last hour' is implied to the API. Wrong because the endpoint defaults to a short window when `from`/`to` are absent. Avoidable by computing `now-1h`..`now` and passing both bounds explicitly.
impact: The agent reported 4 errors when there were 130 in the hour, masking an ongoing spike.
correct_action: Set `filter.from=now-1h` and `filter.to=now` (or epoch ms) on the logs query before aggregating.
recovery_plan: Notice the result count looked too low for an active incident
Re-run the query with explicit `from`/`to` covering the hour
Compare new count against the timeseries
Report the corrected error volume
Save the query with a bound time range
evaluation_criteria: Checks explicit time bounds were passed matching the request
Verifies the result window covers the requested hour
Flags reliance on default time windows

task: Memoize an expensive React component callback
user_request: Stop the chart from re-rendering on every keystroke.
agent_action: Agent wrapped the handler in `useCallback(fn)` but omitted the dependency array argument entirely, so the callback was recreated on every render and the memoization had no effect.
root_cause: `useCallback(fn, deps)` only memoizes when given a `deps` array; called as `useCallback(fn)` it returns a new function each render.
why_it_failed: Assumption: `useCallback` caches by default. Wrong because without the second `deps` argument React cannot know when to reuse the function, so it never does. Avoidable by passing the explicit dependency array, e.g. `[query]`.
impact: The chart kept re-rendering on each keystroke; the intended performance fix did nothing and reviewers nearly merged it.
correct_action: Provide the dependency array: `useCallback(fn, [query])`, including exactly the referenced variables.
recovery_plan: Profile renders and see the callback identity changing
Add the `deps` array to `useCallback`
Confirm the memoized child stops re-rendering
Add an eslint-plugin-react-hooks exhaustive-deps check
Re-profile to confirm the fix
evaluation_criteria: Checks a dependency array was supplied to the memo hook
Verifies the listed deps match referenced variables
Flags memo hooks called without deps

task: Install a Helm chart into the staging release
user_request: Upgrade the redis chart in staging.
agent_action: Agent ran `helm upgrade redis bitnami/redis` without `-f values-staging.yaml`, so the upgrade dropped all staging-specific overrides and reverted to chart defaults.
root_cause: `helm upgrade` without `-f`/`--values` (and without `--reuse-values`) applies only chart defaults, discarding the environment override file the release was installed with.
why_it_failed: Assumption: helm preserves prior custom values automatically. Wrong because upgrades reset to defaults unless `-f values-staging.yaml` or `--reuse-values` is supplied. Avoidable by passing the staging values file used at install time.
impact: Staging Redis came up with default 256Mi memory and no persistence, evicting cached sessions until corrected.
correct_action: Run `helm upgrade redis bitnami/redis -f values-staging.yaml` (or `--reuse-values`) so staging overrides persist.
recovery_plan: Diff rendered values with `helm get values redis`
Re-run upgrade with `-f values-staging.yaml`
Verify resource limits and persistence are restored
Confirm pods are healthy
Document required values flag in the deploy guide
evaluation_criteria: Checks the environment values file was supplied on upgrade
Verifies prior overrides were preserved or reapplied
Flags upgrades that silently revert to chart defaults

task: Deduplicate a Snowflake MERGE upsert
user_request: Upsert the daily orders into the orders_dim table.
agent_action: Agent wrote a `MERGE INTO orders_dim USING staging_orders` but omitted the `ON` join predicate's business key (matched only on a nullable `email`), so rows with null email all collided and overwrote each other.
root_cause: The MERGE `ON` clause lacked the required `order_id` key; matching only on a nullable column caused unintended matches and lost updates.
why_it_failed: Assumption: email uniquely identifies an order row. Wrong because email is nullable and non-unique; the durable key `order_id` was left out of `ON`. Avoidable by joining on `target.order_id = source.order_id`.
impact: Multiple distinct orders with null email merged into one row, silently dropping ~600 orders from the dimension.
correct_action: Match the MERGE on the primary business key `order_id` (and assert it is non-null in staging) before applying.
recovery_plan: Compare staging vs target row counts and spot the shortfall
Rewrite the MERGE `ON` to use `order_id`
Validate keys are non-null in staging first
Re-run the merge into a fresh table and reconcile counts
Backfill the dropped orders
evaluation_criteria: Checks the MERGE join uses a complete non-null business key
Verifies post-merge row counts reconcile with source
Flags merges keyed on nullable/non-unique columns

task: Make a feature-store fetch reproducible
user_request: Pull training features for the churn model.
agent_action: Agent called `feature_store.get_historical_features(entity_df, features)` without passing `full_feature_names` or a `point_in_time` timestamp column in `entity_df`, so it joined latest values and leaked future data into training.
root_cause: Point-in-time-correct joins require an event-timestamp column in `entity_df`; omitting it makes the store return current feature values, leaking the label horizon.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the feature store returns historically-correct values by default. Wrong because without an event timestamp it returns latest values, causing target leakage. Avoidable by including an `event_timestamp` per entity row.
impact: The churn model trained on leaked future features, showing 0.94 offline AUC that collapsed to 0.61 in production.
correct_action: Add an `event_timestamp` column to `entity_df` so the store performs a point-in-time-correct join.
recovery_plan: Notice train/serve AUC gap signaling leakage
Add event_timestamp to entity_df
Re-pull features with point-in-time join
Retrain and re-evaluate offline vs online
Add a leakage check to the pipeline
evaluation_criteria: Checks a point-in-time timestamp was provided for historical features
Verifies no future data leaked into training
Flags latest-value joins used for training data

task: List Slack channel members for an audit
user_request: Who's in the #finance-private channel?
agent_action: Agent called `slack.conversations.members` with the channel ID but omitted the `cursor` param on subsequent calls, returning only the first 100 members and reporting that as the full roster.
root_cause: `conversations.members` returns `response_metadata.next_cursor`; without passing it on follow-up calls the result is capped at the first page.
why_it_failed: Assumption: one call returns all members. Wrong because the API paginates at 100 and returns a `next_cursor`. Avoidable by looping while `next_cursor` is non-empty.
impact: An access audit of a sensitive finance channel under-reported membership, missing 40 of 180 members.
correct_action: Loop `conversations.members` passing `cursor=next_cursor` until it is empty, then aggregate all member IDs.
recovery_plan: Compare member count against admin console total
Re-run with cursor pagination to completion
Aggregate all member pages
Re-issue the audit report
Add a count assertion against the directory
evaluation_criteria: Checks the cursor was passed across pages
Verifies the member count is complete vs source of truth
Flags single-page results treated as complete

task: Create a Grafana alert rule with evaluation window
user_request: Alert when p99 latency on the gateway exceeds 500ms.
agent_action: Agent created the alert rule via the Grafana API with the condition expression but omitted the `for` duration field, so the alert fired instantly on a single momentary spike instead of after sustained breach.
root_cause: A Grafana alert without a `for` pending period evaluates as immediately firing on any single breaching sample, producing flapping alerts.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the alert needs only a threshold condition. Wrong because without `for` (e.g. `for: 5m`) any transient spike pages immediately. Avoidable by setting a pending period matching the SLO.
impact: On-call was paged 18 times overnight by transient p99 spikes that self-resolved within seconds.
correct_action: Set `for: 5m` (or appropriate) so the alert fires only after a sustained threshold breach.
recovery_plan: Review alert history showing rapid flapping
Add a `for` pending duration to the rule
Re-deploy and silence during the change
Observe that transient spikes no longer page
Tune duration against SLO burn
evaluation_criteria: Checks a pending/for duration was set on the alert
Verifies the alert no longer fires on single samples
Flags threshold-only rules without sustained-breach windows

task: Tag a Datadog monitor for routing
user_request: Create a monitor for the payments queue depth.
agent_action: Agent created the monitor via `datadog.monitors.create` with a query and message but omitted the `tags` and the `@`-mention notification handle, so no team was notified when it triggered.
root_cause: Datadog routes notifications via `@`-handles inside the message and routes ownership via `tags`; both were absent, so the monitor alerted into the void.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating a monitor automatically notifies the owning team. Wrong because Datadog only notifies handles explicitly referenced in the message. Avoidable by including `@slack-payments` and `team:payments` tags.
impact: Queue depth crossed threshold for 40 minutes with no page; the backlog was found only by a customer complaint.
correct_action: Include an `@`-mention notification target in the message and `team:payments` tags when creating the monitor.
recovery_plan: Audit the monitor and find no notification target
Edit to add `@slack-payments` and ownership tags
Trigger a test notification
Confirm the team receives it
Add a creation template requiring notify handles
evaluation_criteria: Checks a notification target was included on the monitor
Verifies ownership tags were set
Flags monitors created with no notify handle

task: Export a Prometheus range query for a dashboard
user_request: Get CPU usage for the web pods over the last 6 hours.
agent_action: Agent hit the Prometheus `/api/v1/query_range` endpoint with the query, `start`, and `end` but omitted the required `step` parameter, so the API returned a 400 and the agent reported 'no data available'.
root_cause: `query_range` requires `step`; without it the endpoint returns HTTP 400 'invalid parameter step', which the agent misread as empty data.
why_it_failed: Assumption: `start`/`end` are sufficient for a range query. Wrong because `query_range` mandates a `step` resolution. Avoidable by passing e.g. `step=60s` and checking the HTTP status before interpreting the body.
impact: The dashboard panel rendered blank and the agent told the user CPU data did not exist, delaying capacity review.
correct_action: Include `step=60s` on the `query_range` call and verify a 200 status before reading results.
recovery_plan: Inspect the HTTP 400 and error message
Add `step` to the request
Re-run and confirm a 200 with samples
Render the panel
Validate sample resolution matches the window
evaluation_criteria: Checks `step` was supplied to query_range
Verifies HTTP status was checked before declaring no data
Flags 400s misreported as empty results

task: Idempotently upload a Slack file once
user_request: Upload the latest report.pdf to #weekly-reports.
agent_action: Agent retried `slack.files.upload` after a timeout without passing any client-side dedupe key or checking prior upload, posting the same file twice in the channel.
root_cause: The upload retry carried no idempotency token or prior-upload check, and `files.upload` is not idempotent, so the second call created a duplicate file.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a timed-out upload did not go through. Wrong because the first call had succeeded server-side. Avoidable by listing recent files / using a stable client dedupe key before retrying.
impact: Two identical weekly reports appeared in the channel, confusing recipients about which was canonical and requiring manual cleanup.
correct_action: Before retrying, query `files.list` for the same filename/timestamp or carry a dedupe key, and only upload if absent.
recovery_plan: Detect duplicate via files.list
Delete the redundant upload with files.delete
Add a pre-retry existence check
Re-run with a dedupe guard
Confirm only one file remains
evaluation_criteria: Checks a dedupe/idempotency guard preceded the retry
Verifies no duplicate artifact was created
Flags blind retries of non-idempotent uploads

task: Set up a React Query with a stable cache key
user_request: Cache the product detail fetch by product id.
agent_action: Agent called `useQuery({queryFn})` and omitted the `queryKey` entirely, so React Query could not key the cache and threw, falling back to refetching uncached on every mount.
root_cause: `useQuery` requires a `queryKey`; without it the cache cannot dedupe or persist results per product id.
why_it_failed: Assumption: React Query derives a key from the function. Wrong because the cache key must be explicit (e.g. `['product', id]`). Avoidable by passing `queryKey: ['product', id]`.
impact: Product pages refetched on every navigation and could not share cache, increasing API load and flicker.
correct_action: Provide `queryKey: ['product', id]` so results cache and dedupe per product.
recovery_plan: Reproduce the missing-key error/refetch
Add an explicit `queryKey` including the id
Confirm cache hits across navigations
Add a lint rule for query keys
Verify reduced network calls
evaluation_criteria: Checks an explicit query key including the id was supplied
Verifies cache reuse across mounts
Flags queries lacking a stable key

task: Scope a kubectl delete to avoid mass deletion
user_request: Clean up the failed test pods in the ci namespace.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl -n ci delete pods --all` but omitted the `--field-selector=status.phase=Failed` filter, deleting every pod including running CI jobs, not just the failed ones.
root_cause: `delete pods --all` without a `--field-selector` or label selector targets the entire namespace, not the failed subset the user intended.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'clean up failed pods' is conveyed by intent. Wrong because the command had no selector restricting it to `status.phase=Failed`. Avoidable by adding `--field-selector=status.phase=Failed`.
impact: Running CI jobs were killed mid-run, forcing reruns of the entire pipeline for 12 in-flight PRs.
correct_action: Run `kubectl -n ci delete pods --field-selector=status.phase=Failed` so only failed pods are removed.
recovery_plan: Recognize running pods were deleted
Notify CI owners and re-trigger affected pipelines
Re-run deletes with the field-selector only
Add a confirmation/selector guard to the runbook
Audit for any lost job artifacts
evaluation_criteria: Checks a phase/label selector scoped the deletion
Verifies running workloads were not affected
Flags `--all` deletes without a restricting filter

task: Train/test split with a fixed seed
user_request: Split the dataset 80/20 for the experiment.
agent_action: Agent called `train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2)` but omitted `random_state`, so each pipeline run produced a different split and metrics were not reproducible across reruns.
root_cause: `train_test_split` shuffles with a nondeterministic seed unless `random_state` is set, making the split irreproducible.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the split is stable across runs. Wrong because without `random_state` the shuffle differs each call. Avoidable by passing `random_state=42`.
impact: Two engineers reported different model accuracies for 'the same' experiment, wasting a day reconciling the gap.
correct_action: Pass `random_state=42` (or a configured seed) to make the split deterministic and reproducible.
recovery_plan: Notice non-reproducible metrics across runs
Add `random_state` to the split
Re-run and confirm identical splits/metrics
Pin the seed in the experiment config
Document reproducibility requirement
evaluation_criteria: Checks a fixed random seed was supplied for the split
Verifies reruns produce identical splits
Flags nondeterministic splits in experiments

task: Filter a BigQuery JOIN to one tenant
user_request: Sum revenue for tenant acme from the orders and refunds tables.
agent_action: Agent joined `orders` to `refunds` on `order_id` but omitted the `tenant_id = 'acme'` predicate on the refunds side, so cross-tenant refunds were subtracted from Acme's revenue.
failure_type: Omitted tenant filter on one side
root_cause: The tenant predicate was applied to `orders` but not to `refunds`; since `order_id` is unique only per tenant, the unfiltered join matched other tenants' refunds.
why_it_failed: Assumption: filtering one side of the join is enough. Wrong because `order_id` collides across tenants, so the refunds side needed its own `tenant_id` filter. Avoidable by adding `refunds.tenant_id='acme'` (or joining on the composite key).
impact: Acme's reported net revenue was understated by ~$12K from refunds belonging to other tenants.
correct_action: Add `refunds.tenant_id='acme'` (or join on `(tenant_id, order_id)`) so only Acme refunds are subtracted.
recovery_plan: Reconcile the total against the orders-only figure
Add the tenant predicate to the refunds side
Re-run and compare net revenue
Validate against a single-tenant control query
Add a test for cross-tenant leakage
evaluation_criteria: Checks the tenant filter was applied to every joined table
Verifies cross-tenant rows did not contaminate the aggregate
Flags single-sided filters on multi-tenant joins

task: Configure an early-stopping callback
user_request: Add early stopping so training halts when val loss plateaus.
agent_action: Agent added `EarlyStopping(monitor='val_loss')` but omitted the `patience` argument and the run used the default `patience=0`, so training stopped after the first non-improving epoch.
root_cause: With `patience` unset (defaulting to 0), early stopping halts at the first epoch without improvement, well before a real plateau.
why_it_failed: Assumption: early stopping waits for a sustained plateau by default. Wrong because the default patience is 0 epochs. Avoidable by setting `patience=5` to tolerate noisy non-improvements.
impact: The model stopped at epoch 3 underfit; offline F1 was 0.12 below the expected converged value.
correct_action: Set an explicit `patience` (e.g. `patience=5`) and `min_delta` so training tolerates short plateaus.
recovery_plan: Notice training halted far too early
Set explicit `patience` and `min_delta`
Re-run training to convergence
Compare metrics against the prior underfit run
Pin callback params in config
evaluation_criteria: Checks `patience` was explicitly configured
Verifies training was allowed to converge
Flags early stopping with default zero patience

task: Aria-label an icon-only button in React
user_request: Make the close (X) icon button accessible.
agent_action: Agent rendered `<button onClick={onClose}><XIcon/></button>` but omitted the `aria-label` attribute, so screen readers announced an unlabeled button.
root_cause: An icon-only button conveys no accessible name without `aria-label` (or visually-hidden text); the prop was simply absent.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the SVG icon provides an accessible name. Wrong because decorative icons expose no text to assistive tech. Avoidable by adding `aria-label="Close"`.
impact: Screen-reader users heard 'button' with no purpose; the dialog failed a WCAG name-role-value audit.
correct_action: Add `aria-label="Close"` (or visually-hidden text) to the icon-only button.
recovery_plan: Run an a11y audit (axe) and find the unnamed control
Add `aria-label` to the button
Re-run axe to confirm the violation clears
Add a lint rule for icon-only buttons
Verify with a screen reader
evaluation_criteria: Checks an accessible name was provided for the icon button
Verifies the a11y audit passes
Flags icon-only controls lacking labels

task: Scope an OAuth token for the Slack search call
user_request: Search our Slack for messages mentioning 'rollback'.
agent_action: Agent called `slack.search.messages` using a bot token that lacked the `search:read` scope and never requested it, so every call returned `missing_scope` and the agent reported 'no results'.
root_cause: `search.messages` requires a user token with `search:read`; the request omitted that scope and used a bot token, returning `missing_scope`.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the existing bot token can search messages. Wrong because search requires a user token with `search:read`, which was never granted. Avoidable by checking required scopes and requesting `search:read` on a user token.
impact: The rollback investigation found nothing and stalled, even though matching messages existed.
correct_action: Use a user token granted the `search:read` scope (re-authorize if needed) before calling `search.messages`.
recovery_plan: Inspect the `missing_scope` error in the response
Identify the required `search:read` scope
Re-authorize a user token with that scope
Re-run the search
Confirm matching messages now return
evaluation_criteria: Checks the required scope was present/requested
Verifies the error response was read rather than reported as empty
Flags scope-deficient calls treated as no-result

task: Annotate a Grafana panel for a deploy marker
user_request: Add an annotation at 14:00 UTC for the v2.7 deploy.
agent_action: Agent posted to the Grafana annotations API with `text` and `time` but omitted the `dashboardUID`/`panelId`, so the annotation became a global org annotation not attached to the intended dashboard panel.
root_cause: Without `dashboardUID` and `panelId`, Grafana files the annotation at the organization scope rather than on the specific panel.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the annotation attaches to the dashboard in context. Wrong because the API needs explicit `dashboardUID`/`panelId` to scope it. Avoidable by passing both target IDs.
impact: The deploy marker did not appear on the latency dashboard, so the on-call could not correlate the regression to the release.
correct_action: Include `dashboardUID` and `panelId` so the annotation lands on the intended panel.
recovery_plan: Notice the marker missing from the panel
Delete the mis-scoped global annotation
Re-create it with `dashboardUID` and `panelId`
Confirm it renders on the panel at 14:00 UTC
Template the annotation call with target IDs
evaluation_criteria: Checks target dashboard/panel IDs were supplied
Verifies the annotation rendered on the intended panel
Flags annotations created at the wrong scope

task: Window a Snowflake query to a warehouse
user_request: Run the heavy revenue report query.
agent_action: Agent submitted the report query over a session that had no `WAREHOUSE` set (the role's default was suspended/none), so the query failed with 'No active warehouse selected' and the agent reported the SQL as broken.
root_cause: Snowflake requires an active warehouse to execute; the session omitted `USE WAREHOUSE` and had no default, raising compilation-time 'No active warehouse selected'.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a warehouse was implicitly active for the session. Wrong because the role had no default warehouse set. Avoidable by issuing `USE WAREHOUSE reporting_wh` (or setting it in the connection) before the query.
impact: The revenue report never ran and was misdiagnosed as a SQL bug, delaying the finance close by an hour.
correct_action: Run `USE WAREHOUSE reporting_wh;` (or set `warehouse` in the connection) before executing the report.
recovery_plan: Read the 'No active warehouse selected' error
Set the warehouse with `USE WAREHOUSE`
Re-run the report query
Confirm results return
Set a default warehouse on the role/connection
evaluation_criteria: Checks a warehouse context was set before query execution
Verifies the error was diagnosed as missing context, not bad SQL
Flags queries run without an active warehouse

task: Filter Prometheus alert query to a job
user_request: Alert on high error rate for the api job only.
agent_action: Agent wrote the recording rule `sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]))` but omitted the `job="api"` label matcher, so it summed 5xx across every job and fired on unrelated services.
root_cause: The metric selector lacked the `job="api"` matcher, so the aggregation spanned all jobs instead of the api service.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the metric is already scoped to the api service. Wrong because `http_requests_total` is shared across jobs and needed an explicit `job="api"` matcher. Avoidable by adding the label filter to the selector.
impact: The api error-rate alert fired on a noisy batch job's 5xx, causing a misrouted page and masking the real api signal.
correct_action: Add the `job="api"` label matcher to the metric selector so the rule scopes to the api service only.
